trees.note: Expletive it is not a controller; the to-infinitive is an extraposed subject and move is intransitive.

trees.sentence: They expected the bear to dance
trees.note: Type I expected takes one clausal complement with an overt subject NP; the clause is not dominated by an NP node.

trees.sentence: They persuaded the bear to dance
trees.note: Type II persuaded takes an object NP and a clause with a controlled covert subject; the object NP controls that subject.

book_flags: A non-finite clause has no tensed verb; main clauses remain finite.
Covert NPs may be free (general, non-specific reference) or controlled by an overt constituent in a higher clause. Controlled gaps, including movement gaps, are co-indexed.
The four non-finite verb forms are bare infinitive, to-infinitive, passive participle, and -ing participle.
The infinitive particle to is represented as a [-tense] auxiliary; MOD does not occur in non-finite clauses, while PERF, PROG, and PASS may occur.
In non-finite relatives, the wh-expression in C2 is covert; relative clauses are restrictive and modify NOM. Bare infinitives are excluded from non-finite relative clauses.

When a non-finite clause complements a verb, the old six-way V subcategorisation and NP node are not used for the clause complement. Type I verbs take one clause with an overt subject; Type II verbs take an NP plus a clause with a controlled covert subject.
Promise is Type II but its lower covert subject is controlled by the higher subject, unlike the usual Type II pattern where the object controls it.
